title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Word K-Periodic
summary: Given a string word of length n divisible by k, you can perform operations to make word k-periodic.
statement: Given a string word of length n divisible by k, you can perform operations to make word k-periodic. In one operation, select any two indices i and j divisible by k, then replace the substring of length k starting at i with the substring starting at j. The goal is to find the minimum number of operations needed to achieve a k-periodic word, where a word is k-periodic if it can be formed by repeating a substring of length k.
constraints: word is nonempty, k is positive, and its length is divisible by k.
One operation replaces any aligned length-k block with a copy of another aligned block.
Return the minimum operations needed to make every block equal.
hints: The final period must equal one of the existing aligned blocks, because operations only copy blocks.
Count block frequencies and retain the most common block, replacing every other block once.
Split at multiples of k; return numberOfBlocks-maximumFrequency.
Choosing a block with frequency f costs total-f, so maximizing f minimizes operations and is achievable by copying that block.
